title: Number bonds to ten on your fingers
examples: How do I learn number bonds to ten?

explain.say: Hold up both hands. You have ten fingers: a ready-made maths tool! Number bonds to ten are pairs of numbers that make ten. Look at the board: seven and three fill the frame.

draw.text: Number bonds to ten on your fingers

explain.say: Put down four fingers. How many are still up? Six! So six and four make ten. Look at the board: six counters, then four more. Full! Can you wiggle the four fingers you put down?
Now put down just two fingers. Eight are still up. Eight and two make ten. See the eight and the two on the board? Can you say it with me: eight and two make ten?
Here is a special one: five and five. One whole hand and the other whole hand! Each row of the frame holds five. Can you give yourself a high five?

Look at all the pairs on the board. Each pair makes ten, and you can turn them around too. Amazing! Your brain learns in its own way, and lots of brilliant people learn like this. Can you show every pair on your fingers?

faq.q: What is a number bond to ten?
faq.a: It is a pair of numbers that add up to ten, like seven and three, or six and four.

faq.q: How do I use my fingers for number bonds?
faq.a: Hold up ten fingers and put some down. The fingers down and the fingers still up are a pair that makes ten.

faq.q: Why learn number bonds to ten?
faq.a: They make adding and taking away much faster. If you know seven and three make ten, you also know ten take away three is seven.

faq.q: What are all the number bonds to ten?
faq.a: Zero and ten, one and nine, two and eight, three and seven, four and six, and five and five. Plus all of those turned around.
asks: List the number bonds to ten

faq.q: How can I practise number bonds?
faq.a: Play finger flash: a grown-up shows some fingers, and you say how many more make ten. Or use a ten frame with counters.

facts: Not counting turn-arounds, there are six pairs that make ten: 0 and 10, 1 and 9, 2 and 8, 3 and 7, 4 and 6, and 5 and 5.
Adding works in any order: 7 + 3 and 3 + 7 both make 10.

quiz.say: Which number goes with 6 to make 10?

wrong.1: Six and three make nine, one short of ten.
wrong.2: Six and five make eleven, one too many.

quiz.say: You hold up 10 fingers and put 2 down. How many are still up?
quiz.why: Ten take away two is eight, because eight and two make ten.

wrong.1: Seven would mean three fingers went down.
wrong.2: Two is how many went down, not how many are up.
